title: Object Detection: Boxes, Anchors & Modern Detectors
interviewAnswer: Object detection predicts both classes and locations. Two-stage detectors separate proposals and classification; one-stage detectors predict densely. Modern detectors may be anchor-based or anchor-free, but all require localization and classification reasoning.
keyPoints: Bounding-box regression and classification are separate losses/signals.
NMS or set-prediction logic resolves duplicate detections.
why: Object Detection: Boxes, Anchors & Modern Detectors is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
intuition: Bounding-box regression and classification are separate losses/signals.
deepDive: Object detection predicts both classes and locations. Two-stage detectors separate proposals and classification; one-stage detectors predict densely. Modern detectors may be anchor-based or anchor-free, but all require localization and classification reasoning. NMS or set-prediction logic resolves duplicate detections. Small-object performance depends on resolution/features. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: Detect construction tools in site images with class labels and bounding boxes rather than one label per image.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.

production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.
